Minimum practice: Hold out whole source studies (or laboratories); report random-split metrics only as a reference
Why (evidence in this study): Random splits overstated accuracy about two-fold (Table 2)

Minimum practice: Fix a list of held-out studies before modelling and evaluate it once
Why (evidence in this study): Locked results were worse than development CV (Table 6)

Minimum practice: Audit identical runs reported in several studies before splitting
Report per-study errors and the mean-predictor baseline next to pooled R²
Why (evidence in this study): Pooled metrics were dominated by a few studies (Section 3.8)

Minimum practice: Calibrate prediction intervals across studies, not across random runs
Support claims about effects of conditions or optimal conditions with held-out-study contrasts or rankings
Why (evidence in this study): Within-study changes and rankings did not transfer (Sections 3.4–3.5)

Minimum practice: Recommend 1–3 local runs and report the anchored error
Why (evidence in this study): Three runs reduced the median error by 3–4 wt% (Table 5)

Minimum practice: Record product-recovery solvent, yield basis, fraction definitions, mass-balance closure and reactor details in curated databases
Why (evidence in this study): Coarse parsed descriptors did not explain offsets (Table 3)

Minimum practice: Release code, the held-out study list and per-run predictions
